title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Lesotho: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Lesotho: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Lesotho: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Organizing medical, pension, and legal affairs during a serious or terminal illness in Lesotho centers on coordinating palliative and clinical care, executing a compliant will or power of attorney under the 2024 inheritance statute, filing disability or ill-health claims on time, and apostilling records required abroad. Because central government subdomains including the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Foreign Affairs experience external timeouts or TLS validation failures, this guide uses verified Ministry of Home Affairs NICR pages, PODCPF, Parliament of Lesotho documentation, StarLight Oasis of Hope Hospice, Partners In Health Lesotho, HCCH authority records, and LesLII.

steps.title: Clinical Records and Palliative Care Support
steps.html:
• Request certified hospital clinical summaries, diagnostic reports, and attending physician statements confirming prognosis and work incapacity, as both employers and pension boards rely on medical proof [3][4].
  • Coordinate home-based palliative nursing, pain management, and holistic patient support through StarLight Oasis of Hope Hospice, and access regional clinic care through Partners In Health Lesotho in Maseru West and partner districts [9][10].

steps.title: Powers of Attorney and Will Formalities under the 2024 Act
steps.html:
• Prepare a written Power of Attorney while full legal capacity remains so a designated representative can manage banking, property, and civil paperwork on the patient's behalf.
  • Draft a valid written will satisfying the Administration of Estates and Inheritance Act, 2024 (Act No. 2 of 2024, operational from 2 April 2024), which repealed the 1935 Proclamation and customary sole-heir rules and unified estate governance under the Master of the High Court [5][6].
  • Ensure the testator signs the bottom of every page in the simultaneous presence of at least two independent competent witnesses aged 18 or over, who must sign in each other's presence and record their full names and national ID numbers alongside a clear date and revocation clause [5][6].

steps.title: Pension Disability Benefits and Beneficiary Nominations
steps.html:
• Public officers permanently incapacitated from duty should notify the Public Officers' Defined Contribution Pension Fund (PODCPF) within the mandatory 6-month notification window to apply for medical disability or ill-health retirement benefits [3][4].
  • Submit medical board findings and supporting identity documents via PODCPF claim procedures, and file an updated beneficiary nomination form so fund allocations align with the member's wishes [3][4].
  • Private-sector employees and private policy holders should similarly confirm medical-incapacity triggers and beneficiary designations directly with employers and insurers.

steps.title: Civil Identity and Household Asset Dossier
steps.html:
• Verify that national ID and civil status records with the Ministry of Home Affairs (NICR) match current names and marital status, preventing delays in future legal or financial transfers [1][2].
  • Assemble an organized folder containing original title deeds, bank account details, PODCPF member numbers, tax references, chieftaincy or marriage records, and the storage location of any executed will [6].

steps.title: Cross-Border Document Authentication (Hague Apostille)
steps.html:
• Lesotho is a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (in force since 4 October 1966 by succession), meaning notarized powers of attorney, certified civil records, and authenticated medical reports need only an Apostille for use in other Convention member states [7][11].
  • Obtain Apostilles through Lesotho's designated Competent Authorities listed with HCCH, including the Attorney-General, Permanent Secretary of a Ministry or Department, Registrar of the High Court, Resident Magistrate, or Magistrate of the First Class [7][8].

contacts.name: Public Officers' Defined Contribution Pension Fund (PODCPF)
contacts.note: 4th Floor Pension Fund House, Constitution Road, Maseru (Toll Free 80002778); disability claims within 6 months and beneficiary updates.

contacts.name: Ministry of Home Affairs (NICR)
contacts.note: Corner Moshoeshoe and Lerotholi Roads, Maseru; civil identity verification and vital records.

contacts.name: Registrar of the High Court
contacts.note: Designated HCCH Apostille Competent Authority alongside the Attorney-General and Magistrates; High Court supervises Master of the High Court estate registries.

contacts.name: StarLight Oasis of Hope Hospice
contacts.note: Home-based palliative care, pain relief coordination, and patient family support in Lesotho.

contacts.note: House 233, Corner Lancers and Caldwell Roads, Maseru West; clinical care coordination.
